pull.title: feat(models): bulk visibility — one glob per provider, selection, facets, undo
pull.body:
# The Models page learns to manage a thousand models

Provider-level **Show all / Hide all / Invert**, per-row selection with range
picking (Shift+click, Shift+Arrow, drag), state facets, a bulk action bar and
Undo — one request per gesture instead of one per model.

## What was wrong (measured, on the real install)

1021 models across 10 providers; `nous_portal` alone has 317.

| Task | Before |
|---|---|
| Hide every `nous_portal` model | 1 open + 7 "Show more" + **317 ticks = 325 interactions** |
| …requests | **634** |
| …bytes | **≈ 1.07 GB** (the whole 3.4 MB catalogue re-fetched after every tick) |
| …wall clock, network alone | **≈ 5–9 minutes** |
| Patterns written into `MODEL_VISIBILITY_DENY` | **317** |
| Invert a provider | **no path existed** |
| Hide the 38 models matching `opus` across 4 providers | **43 interactions**, and you had to find the 4 providers by eye |
| Undo a mis-aimed bulk hide | **N re-ticks** |
| Sticky elements in the view | **0** — the provider name sat 15,655 px above the last row |

And it was not merely slow: the toggle route read the pattern lists and
computed their replacement **outside** the config lock, so two toggles racing
each other each wrote a full pair derived from the same base. Last writer wins;
the first pattern vanished. Firing N toggles from the client was a *lossy*
implementation of "hide all", not just a slow one.

## What to expect now

| Task | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hide a 317-model provider | 325 interactions | **2** (the second is an inline confirm for ≥200 models) |
| …requests / bytes / time | 634 / ~1.07 GB / 5–9 min | **1 / 41 KB / 7 ms** |
| …patterns written | 317 | **1** (`nous_portal/*`) |
| Hide the 38 `opus` matches | 43 | **3** — type, `Select all 38`, `Hide` |
| Invert a provider | impossible | **1** |
| Undo | N re-ticks | **1 click**, restores both lists exactly |
| Sticky provider headers | 0 | **1 per rendered provider** |
| Repaint 317 rows after a bulk result | — | **12 ms**, one DOM pass |
| View nodes, all collapsed / one provider paged to 317 | 98 / 2645 | 175 / 3358 |

- **Selection.** A box in a ruled left gutter on every row, beside the
  visibility tick. Click one and Shift+click another for a range; **Shift+Space**
  and **Shift+ArrowDown / ArrowUp** do the same from the keyboard (walking back
  towards the anchor shrinks the range); **press and drag down the gutter** to
  sweep rows, with every row taking the anchor's new state so a drag never
  leaves a mixed run. A drag that starts anywhere but the gutter selects
  nothing. The provider header's box is tri-state, and the bar counts live.
- **Facets** — All / Visible / Hidden / Configured / Overridden — plus
  `Select all N` on the result-count line that already existed.
- **Feedback.** A persistent `role="status"` panel: what happened, what pattern
  was written or removed, and the un-honoured breakdown grouped so one
  offending glob is named **once**, not 317 times — with `Undo`, `Show the N`
  and `Dismiss`.
- Screenshots: `h-after-models-top.png`, `h-after-provider-header.png`,
  `h-after-selection-bar.png`, `h-after-bulk-result-partial.png`,
  `h-after-facets.png`, `h-after-models-900px.png`. `assets/admin-model-config.png`
  and its in-app twin were re-captured.

## Action required

**None.** Existing exact patterns and existing globs are preserved. `Hide all`
on a provider that already carries `nous_portal/*` is idempotent and reports
that nothing was written. `Show all` removes only `provider/*` and the
wildcard-free refs under it; a glob you typed yourself is never deleted — when
one of them still hides a model, the panel names it rather than quietly
removing it. Hiding remains display-only: a configured-but-hidden ref still
resolves, still serves, and still shows in the pickers.

## Known and deliberate

- **"Hide all" writes one glob, not 317 exact refs.** That is a standing
  statement about the provider, so models it publishes next week are hidden on
  arrival. 317 exact refs encode a snapshot that silently stops applying, and
  they turn a text field you are invited to hand-edit into a 10 KB blob. A
  partial selection, a filtered provider and every `invert` write exact refs
  instead.
- **No confirmation modal.** Visibility is reversible and display-only, and a
  dialog on every "Hide all" is the friction being removed. Actions over 200
  models get one inline confirm step in the button itself.
- **Not a toast.** The toast rule says auto-dismiss in 3–5 s; a report carrying
  a per-pattern breakdown and the only Undo must not vanish on a timer.
- **Two checkboxes per row, always visible.** Selection-mode-on-demand would
  hide the affordance.
- The provider disclosure is now a `<button aria-expanded>` rather than
  `<details>`, because a `<summary>` must be its parent's first child and a
  control inside a `<summary>` is the a11y violation Chrome reported 1,021
  times on the model rows.
- Not done: virtualising the list; merging (rather than clobbering) the pattern
  textareas on `Save patterns`; the hardcoded `of 11` tier denominator; the
  override editor, which is reviewed and deliberately kept.

## Residual risks

1. **The whole-provider glob is a policy the user may not realise they wrote.**
   After `Hide all`, next week's models are hidden on arrival. Named in the
   result panel, the Guide, USAGE and the pattern textarea — not mitigated for
   someone who reads none of them.
2. **`Show all` cannot undo a glob you wrote, and says so instead.** Some users
   will read "nothing changed, your pattern `nous*` still hides these" as the
   button being broken. Deleting patterns we did not write is worse.
3. **The selection is client-side and unversioned.** Between picking 300 refs
   and pressing Hide, another client can change what those refs are. The server
   reports per-ref truth, so nothing is silently wrong, but a stale selection
   can produce a surprising report.
4. **`apply_admin_config_with` is a new lock ordering** — it takes
   `_config_lock` before reading settings, where `apply_admin_config` takes it
   after. Same lock, no other lock involved, so no deadlock is possible, but it
   is a change in the shared config path and deserves a careful read. Both the
   bulk and the single-toggle route use it.
5. **The models bar stacks on the global action bar.** Its offset is now
   measured from `.action-bar` at render time rather than hardcoded (a fixed
   56 px left it half-hidden in the browser drive), but the two bars still have
   no shared token.
6. **The tests for this page are largely string matches on `admin.js`.** The
   new static guards are written so the redesign satisfies them; the only
   existing assertion changed was adding the new path to the endpoint tuple.
7. **Two checkboxes per row is a legibility bet** validated by the author's
   judgement and one browser drive. The cheap fallback is
   selection-mode-on-demand.
8. **jsdom can silently skip.** Here it **ran**: 95 passed in
   `test_admin_static_jsdom.py`, 21 of them new and models-scoped.

## Baseline

Full suite on this branch: **`15 failed, 7526 passed, 38 skipped in 148.00s`** —
exactly the pre-existing baseline (8 websearch env-file, 6 PowerShell
installer, `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`).
Nothing new. ruff format/check, repo-wide `ty`, and the suppression grep are
clean. Version `6.6.0` → `6.7.0` (MINOR: new endpoint and capability, no env
var added, removed or renamed) with `uv lock` in the same commit.

commit.message:
feat(models): bulk visibility — one glob per provider, selection, facets, undo (#H)

Hiding one provider's models cost 325 interactions, 634 requests and about a
gigabyte of JSON. Measured on the live install (1021 models across 10
providers, `nous_portal` = 317): one provider open, seven "Show more" clicks,
then 317 ticks, and `toggleModelVisibility` (admin.js:11530-11550) re-fetched
the entire 3.4 MB catalogue after every single one — five to nine minutes of
network for one intent. There was no bulk control, no selection, no invert, no
undo, and nothing sticky in the view, so a user thirty rows down had no
on-screen answer to "which provider am I in".

Worse than slow: it was lossy. `toggle_model_visibility` read the settings and
computed the replacement allow/deny pair (admin_routes.py:925-928) *outside*
`_config_lock`, so two toggles that read before either committed each wrote a
full pair derived from the same base — last writer wins and the first pattern
silently vanished. Firing N toggles from the client was therefore not a slow
implementation of "hide all"; it was a wrong one.

What the page does now
- Every provider header is sticky and carries `Show all` / `Hide all` /
  `Invert` plus a tri-state select-all box, so the bulk controls are reachable
  without paging the provider in at all — they read `modelsState.data`, never
  rendered rows, so the 40-row lazy fill is untouched.
- Every row has a selection box in a ruled left gutter beside its visibility
  tick. Range selection: Shift+click, Shift+Space, Shift+ArrowDown/Up (walking
  back shrinks the range), and press-and-drag down the gutter. A drag that
  starts anywhere else selects nothing, and the pointer path is never the only
  way in — WCAG 2.2's single-pointer-alternative rule.
- State facets (All / Visible / Hidden / Configured / Overridden) and a
  `Select all N` on the existing result-count line, so "hide the 38 models
  matching opus across four providers" is three interactions.
- One `POST /admin/api/model-admin/visibility/bulk` per gesture, one settings
  commit, and no catalogue refetch: the client patches the payload it already
  holds from the per-ref results.
- A persistent `role="status"` result panel with Undo, `Show the N` and
  Dismiss.

Non-obvious choices
- **"Hide all" on a whole provider writes ONE glob, `nous_portal/*`.** 317
  exact refs encode a snapshot: they stop applying the moment the provider
  publishes a 318th model, and they turn a `<textarea>` the user is invited to
  hand-edit into a 10 KB blob. A glob keeps meaning what it said and costs 1021
  fnmatch calls per page build instead of 324,000. A *partial* selection, a
  filtered provider, and every `invert` write exact refs instead: a closed set
  of hand-picked models is a fact, not a policy, and no glob describes it
  without hiding something the user did not choose.
- **"Show all" removes `P/*` and the wildcard-free refs under it, and nothing
  else.** A glob the user typed (`nous*`, `*:free`) is never deleted on their
  behalf — that edit is unrecoverable and its blast radius is not confined to
  the provider they clicked. What it therefore cannot achieve is *reported*:
  the panel names the offending pattern once, not once per model, gives the
  un-honoured count, and offers to narrow the tree to exactly those refs.
- **Undo without a vanishing toast.** The response carries the previous
  allow/deny pair; Undo posts it to the existing `…/visibility` route — no new
  server state, no token, no TTL. A report that names which of your own globs
  overruled which refs must not disappear on a 3-second timer, so this is a
  dismissible panel rather than the `showMessage` line (which has no queue and
  is overwritten by the next call anyway).
- **Both controls on every row, always.** Selection-mode-on-demand would hide
  the affordance; the two boxes are separated by a ruled gutter cell, by the
  visibility control keeping its word (`Show` / `Hidden`), and by the selection
  box carrying only an `aria-label`.
- **The read-modify-write race is closed on both routes.**
  `apply_admin_config_with(build)` takes `_config_lock` *first* and calls
  `build(current settings)` inside it, so the read and the write are one
  critical section. The single-toggle route uses it too, and no longer claims
  `honored: true` for a write that failed validation.
- The provider disclosure is a `<button aria-expanded>` rather than
  `<details>`: a `<summary>` must be its `<details>`' first child, which leaves
  nowhere legal for a checkbox and three buttons — and a control inside a
  `<summary>` is the a11y violation Chrome reported 1,021 times on the rows.

Verification
- Driven in Chrome against the real 1021-model catalogue (harness serving this
  worktree's admin_static on 8099, GETs proxied to the live 8082, every write
  emulated locally against this PR's own rules; the user's config untouched).
  Hide all `nous_portal`: **2 interactions** (the second is the inline confirm
  step for ≥200 models), **1 request**, **41 KB**, **7 ms** — against 325 / 634
  / ~1.07 GB / 5-9 min. One pattern written (`nous_portal/*`), not 317.
  Repainting 317 rows after a bulk result: 12 ms, single pass. Filter
  keystrokes with a 300-ref selection held: selection intact, no regression.
  Sticky headers: 10 (was 0). View nodes collapsed 175 (was 98); with one
  provider paged to 317 rows 3358 (was 2645); scrollHeight 17098 (was 16823).
  No console errors, no interactive element inside a `<summary>`, no
  unlabelled checkbox, exactly one live region, `/` and `Escape` behave, and at
  900px the bar goes full width and the header un-sticks with no horizontal
  scroll. `Show all` with `nous*` seeded deletes nothing and reports all 17
  un-honoured; with `*:free` it names the pattern once and offers `Show the 6`.
- jsdom: the Models page had **zero** behavioural coverage; the harness now
  stubs `/admin/api/model-admin` with 3 providers x 45 models and the three
  write routes, and 21 new tests cover lazy fill, paging, both controls per
  row, the tri-state box, Shift+click / Shift+Arrow / drag, selection surviving
  a filter rebuild, one-request-no-refetch, the partial report, Undo, facets
  and Escape. They RAN, they did not skip.
- Full suite: `15 failed, 7526 passed, 38 skipped` — exactly the pre-existing
  baseline (8 websearch env-file, 6 PowerShell installer,
  `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`). ruff
  format/check, repo-wide ty, and the suppression grep are clean.

Deliberately not done
No routing change (hiding stays display-only and a configured-but-hidden ref
still resolves, re-pinned at bulk scale). `core/model_visibility.py` is
untouched — its glob engine already did everything this needed. No settings key
added, removed or renamed. The three-state override editor is reviewed and
kept: it is the only control that can express "say nothing" vs "send the key
removed" vs "send this". The list is still not virtualised, `Save patterns`
still clobbers both lists, and the `of 11` tier denominator is still hardcoded.
